verses.text: Thousands of people had gathered, packed so tightly that they were stepping on each other. Jesus began by telling his disciples, “Watch out for the Pharisees’ yeast—that’s their hypocrisy.”
“Nothing covered up will stay hidden; nothing kept secret won’t be uncovered.”
“Whatever you say in the dark will be heard in daylight. What you whisper in a back room will be announced from the rooftops.”
“I’m telling you, my friends: don’t fear people who can kill the body and then can’t do anything else to you.”
“I’ll tell you who to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has authority to throw you into Gehenna. Yes, fear him.”
“Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins? Yet God doesn’t forget a single one.”
“Even the hairs on your head are all counted. So don’t be afraid—you matter more than a whole flock of sparrows.”
“I’m telling you: everyone who acknowledges me in front of people, the Son of Man will acknowledge in front of God’s angels.”
“But whoever disowns me in front of people will be disowned in front of God’s angels.”
“Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man can be forgiven. But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven.”
“When they bring you before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, don’t panic about how to defend yourself or what to say.”
“The Holy Spirit will teach you in that very moment what you need to say.”
Someone in the crowd said to Jesus, “Teacher, tell my brother to split the inheritance with me.”
Jesus answered, “Man, who made me your judge or the one who divides your inheritance?”
He told them, “Watch out. Guard yourselves against greed. A person’s life isn’t measured by how much stuff they own.”
Then Jesus told them a parable: “A rich man’s land produced an abundant harvest.”
“He thought to himself, ‘What am I going to do? I don’t have room to store all my crops.’”
“Then he said, ‘Here’s the plan: I’ll tear down my barns, build bigger ones, and store all my grain and goods there.”
“‘Then I’ll tell myself, “You’ve got plenty saved up for years. Take it easy—eat, drink, and enjoy life.”’”
“But God said to him, ‘You fool! Tonight your life will be demanded from you. Who’s going to get all the things you stored up?’”
“That’s how it goes for anyone who stores up wealth for themselves but isn’t rich toward God.”
Jesus told his disciples, “So I’m telling you: don’t worry about your life—what you’ll eat—or your body—what you’ll wear.”
“Life is more than food, and your body is more than clothes.”
“Think about the ravens: they don’t plant or harvest, they have no storeroom or barn, yet God feeds them. You’re worth so much more than birds!”
“Can any of you add even a tiny amount to your height by worrying?”
“If you can’t do even that little thing, why stress about everything else?”
“Look at how lilies grow. They don’t work or make clothes, but I’m telling you, even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed like one of them.”
“If God dresses the grass in the field—which is here today and tossed into the oven tomorrow—won’t he dress you too, you of little faith?”
“So don’t keep chasing what you’ll eat or drink, and don’t stay worried.”
“The nations of the world chase all those things, but your Father knows you need them.”
“Instead, seek God’s Kingdom, and these things will be given to you too.”
“Don’t be afraid, little flock. Your Father is happy to give you the Kingdom.”
“Sell what you own and give to people in need. Make purses for yourselves that won’t wear out—lasting treasure in heaven, where no thief gets near and no moth destroys.”
“Where your treasure is, that’s where your heart will be too.”
“Be dressed and ready for action, with your lamps burning.”
“Be like servants waiting for their master to return from a wedding feast, ready to open the door as soon as he knocks.”
“Blessed are the servants the master finds awake when he returns. I’m telling you the truth: he’ll dress for work, seat them at the table, and serve them himself.”
“They’re blessed if he comes in the middle of the night or even near dawn and finds them ready.”
“Remember: if a homeowner knew when the thief was coming, they’d stay awake and wouldn’t let their house get broken into.”
“So stay ready too. The Son of Man is coming at an hour you don’t expect.”
Peter asked, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
The Lord said, “Who is the faithful and wise manager? The one his master puts in charge of the household to give everyone their food at the right time.”
“Blessed is that servant if the master returns and finds them doing their job.”
“I’m telling you the truth: the master will put that servant in charge of everything he owns.”
“But suppose that servant thinks, ‘My master’s taking forever,’ and starts beating the men and women servants, eating, drinking, and getting drunk.”
“The master will come on a day the servant doesn’t expect and at an hour they don’t know. He’ll cut the servant in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.”
“The servant who knew the master’s will but didn’t get ready or do what he wanted will receive many blows.”
“But the one who didn’t know and did things deserving punishment will receive fewer blows. Much will be required from everyone given much, and even more will be asked of the one trusted with much.”
“I came to cast fire on the earth, and I wish it were already burning.”
“But I have a baptism to go through, and I’m under great pressure until it’s completed!”
“Do you think I came to bring peace on earth? I’m telling you, no—I came to bring division.”
“From now on, five people in one household will be split: three against two, and two against three.”
“They’ll be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.”
Jesus also said to the crowd, “When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say right away, ‘Rain’s coming,’ and it does.”
“When the south wind blows, you say, ‘It’s going to be scorching,’ and it is.”
“Hypocrites! You know how to read the sky and the land. How come you can’t read what’s happening right now?”
“Why don’t you judge for yourselves what’s right?”

“When you’re going with your opponent to court, do your best to settle things on the way. Otherwise they may drag you before the judge, the judge hand you to the officer, and the officer throw you in prison.”
“I’m telling you, you won’t get out until you’ve paid the very last coin.”
